I will use an instrumental-variables design in which days detained is instrumented with outage_week, the indicator for arrest during one of the 40 weeks in 2011-2014 when jail computer outages delayed every bail hearing by 96 hours, which shifts detention by about 3.8 days for reasons unrelated to the defendant and did not change which judge heard the case. The second stage regresses any formal employment in the year after disposition on instrumented days detained, with court-by-month (and week-of-year) fixed effects and baseline controls (prior_arrests, charge_severity, public_defender, dv_charge, age, prior_earn), and I will report the reduced form, the first stage, and covariate-balance tests comparing outage-week and non-outage-week defendants. I considered judge_leniency, the leave-one-out release rate of the randomly rotating bail judge, but I reject it as an instrument because the county's job-readiness program sets each judge's monthly enrollee count in proportion to that same release rate, so leniency moves later employment directly through program enrollment and the exclusion restriction fails; I will instead use judge_leniency only as a control or for a specification check that explicitly adjusts for program enrollment. The main threat to the outage design is that outage weeks may differ from other weeks in the composition of arrests or in case processing beyond the bail hearing (for example, delayed hearings also delaying disposition), which would violate exclusion, so I will check balance on observables, test whether outage status predicts disposition timing or charge outcomes, and restrict to 2011-2014 where outage status is defined. Because the instrument shifts detention by only a few days, the estimate is a local average treatment effect of marginal detention length, and I will be explicit that it may not extrapolate to long detention spells.

CANDIDATES:
judge_leniency | violated
outage_week | plausible
INSTRUMENT: outage_week

I will estimate the effect of counseling meetings on fourth-quarter employment by two-stage least squares, instrumenting the number of meetings attended in the first 12 weeks with `pilot_office`, the indicator for the 19 American Job Centers randomly drawn in 2015 to add a biweekly session, because the office draw was randomized, it shifts attendance by about 2.4 meetings (a strong first stage), and the memo states the pilot changed nothing else at those offices, which supports exclusion. The outcome is the wage-record employment indicator for the fourth quarter after the claim, the endogenous treatment is meetings attended, and I will include `ssn_odd`, `prior_wage`, `tenure`, `age`, `industry`, `ui_weekly`, `office_dist`, and claim-year (and quarter) fixed effects as covariates; `ssn_odd` must be a control rather than an instrument, since odd-digit assignment also triggered an employer wage subsidy that affects hiring directly, independent of meeting attendance. I will report the reduced-form (intent-to-treat) effect of `pilot_office` alongside the 2SLS estimate, interpreting the latter as a local average treatment effect for claimants whose attendance rose because their office offered extra sessions. The main threat is inference and balance with only 38 office clusters (19 treated): standard errors must be clustered at the office level with a wild cluster bootstrap, and I will check pre-pilot balance of office-level characteristics and claimant covariates across pilot and non-pilot offices. A secondary threat is that the 2.4-meeting increase might not be the only channel (e.g., the pilot could also change counselor caseloads or scheduling), so I will test whether `pilot_office` predicts outcomes among claimants who attended zero meetings. I will also check that claimants cannot sort across offices, using the home-address-based assignment and `office_dist` to confirm that the office is determined by residence rather than choice.

CANDIDATES:
ssn_odd | violated
pilot_office | plausible
office_dist | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: pilot_office

I will estimate the effect of years of charter enrollment on 8th-grade math scores by two-stage least squares, instrumenting enrollment with `second_draw_offer` in the subsample of applicants who did not receive an initial offer and were entered in the city's independent September second draw, with fixed effects for the second-draw cell (school by grade by year) so that comparisons are only among applicants facing the same random draw. The first stage regresses years enrolled on `second_draw_offer` and the cell fixed effects (expected first stage about 0.6 years); the second stage regresses the 8th-grade math score on predicted enrollment, adding `baseline_math`, `frl`, and `parent_college` only for precision and checking covariate balance across second-draw winners and losers as a randomization test. I reject `lottery_offer` as the instrument even though it is randomized and has the stronger first stage, because the district enrolled every initial-offer holder in free after-school math tutoring in grades 6-8 regardless of charter attendance, so the offer moves math scores through a channel other than charter enrollment and the exclusion restriction fails, with no way to separate the tutoring effect since it is perfectly collinear with the offer. Non-experimental candidates such as `dist_charter`, `sibling_charter`, and `n_ranked` reflect residential sorting and family preferences and are not credible as excludable instruments. The estimate is a local average treatment effect for second-draw compliers, a selected group of initial-offer losers who stayed in the pool, so it should be labeled as such rather than generalized to all applicants. The main threat is differential attrition in the outcome: if second-draw winners are more likely to remain in the district and appear in the 8th-grade state test file than losers, the IV estimate is biased, so I will test whether follow-up test-score availability differs by `second_draw_offer` and bound the effect under Lee-type trimming if it does, alongside the weaker first stage and smaller sample that make instrument strength a secondary concern.

CANDIDATES:
lottery_offer | violated
second_draw_offer | plausible
dist_charter | doubtful
sibling_charter | doubtful
n_ranked | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: second_draw_offer

I will estimate the effect of the 2014 household broadband subscription share on district average 11th-grade test scores by two-stage least squares, using crew_order as the instrument within the 104 phase-3 districts, where the broadband office's lottery randomly assigned the number of months between the start of phase 3 and the fiber crew's arrival. Crew order shifts the 2014 subscription share by about 1 percentage point per month of delay and, because it changed only when fiber was installed and not the district's assigned phase, it did not move the timing of the grant-funded school computer labs, so the exclusion restriction is credible. I will not use fiber_phase, despite its public lottery and 4-point-per-phase first stage, because the grant also funded new computer labs at the start of each district's phase, so phase affects test scores through a channel other than household broadband; and I will not use dist_datacenter or rural_share because data-center siting and rurality are tied to income, density, and school quality that affect scores directly. The key variables are the outcome (district average 11th-grade score), the treatment (broadband subscription share in percentage points), the instrument crew_order, and the 2010 baseline covariates median_income, rural_share, per_pupil, college_share, and enroll, which I will use to verify lottery balance and improve precision but on which the design does not rely. The main threat is instrument weakness in a sample of only 104 districts, since the first stage spans at most 11 percentage points, so I will report the first-stage F-statistic and Anderson-Rubin confidence sets and refrain from interpreting the point estimate if the first stage is weak. The resulting estimate is a local effect for phase-3 districts whose fiber arrived during 2013, so it may not generalize to the full 410 districts or to early-phase adopters.

CANDIDATES:
fiber_phase | violated
crew_order | plausible
dist_datacenter | doubtful
rural_share | violated
INSTRUMENT: crew_order

I will estimate the effect of counseling meetings on fourth-quarter employment by two-stage least squares, instrumenting the number of meetings attended in the first 12 weeks with `pilot_office`, the indicator for filing at one of the 19 American Job Centers that the state chose by random draw in 2015 to add a biweekly counseling session on both tracks. The first stage is strong (about 2.4 extra meetings), assignment was a lottery across offices, and the memo states the pilot changed nothing else at those offices, so the exclusion restriction is credible; I will report the ITT alongside the LATE, cluster standard errors by office, and add randomization inference over office assignments because there are only 38 clusters. I will include `ssn_odd`, `prior_wage`, `tenure`, `age`, `ui_weekly`, `industry`, `office_dist`, and claim year as covariates after checking that they are balanced across pilot and non-pilot offices, and I will restrict the sample to claims filed after the pilot began in 2015. I reject `ssn_odd` as an instrument even though odd/even SSN track assignment is as good as random and moves attendance by 3.1 meetings: high-track claimants carry the HT flag from the day they file, and the commerce department pays employers a three-month wage subsidy for hiring any HT-flagged claimant, so track assignment raises employment through a channel other than counseling and the exclusion restriction fails. I also considered `office_dist` as a cost-of-attendance instrument but reject it, since distance to the assigned center reflects rural residence and local labor-market conditions that affect re-employment directly. The main threat is that with only 19 treated offices, chance imbalance in local labor markets or claimant composition could bias the estimate and conventional cluster-robust inference is unreliable, so I will pre-specify balance tests and permutation-based p-values, and I will check robustness to dropping offices with the 2015 data-entry delays.

CANDIDATES:
pilot_office | plausible
ssn_odd | violated
office_dist | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: pilot_office

I will estimate the effect of years in a voucher-subsidized unit before age 18 on age-26 earnings by two-stage least squares within the subsample of families offered a voucher (voucher_lottery = 1), using intake_team as the instrument for the treatment. Because the housing authority's software routed lease-up paperwork to the fast second team at random, intake_team should be independent of family characteristics and potential outcomes, and it has a strong first stage (about 2.0 additional years in a voucher unit), so 2SLS identifies the local average treatment effect for children whose families leased up only because processing took 2 weeks instead of 9. I will check randomization by testing balance of hh_income97, n_children, tract_poverty, parent_employed, child_age97, and public_housing across intake teams, include those covariates for precision, report the first stage and reduced form alongside the IV estimate, and cluster standard errors by family since siblings share one assignment. I will not use voucher_lottery as an instrument: although the waitlist draw was random and moves voucher years by 4.2, in 2003 the county workforce board enrolled a parent from every offered family in a free two-year job-training program regardless of voucher use, so the offer affects children's earnings through a channel other than voucher years and violates the exclusion restriction; the lottery yields only an intention-to-treat effect of the bundled offer-plus-training package. Restricting to offered families holds the job-training exposure constant, so it cannot confound the intake_team comparison. The main threat is the exclusion restriction for intake_team itself: faster processing could affect children through channels other than years subsidized (for example, the quality or location of units families could secure before the voucher expired, or reduced stress during the search), and if the software's routing was in fact correlated with application timing or office, randomization would fail, so I will test balance on baseline covariates and application characteristics and interpret the estimate as applying to the marginal lease-up families.

CANDIDATES:
voucher_lottery | violated
intake_team | plausible
INSTRUMENT: intake_team

I will estimate the effect of pretrial detention on post-disposition employment with a two-stage least squares design that uses the recurring jail computer outages as a natural experiment: `outage_week` instruments days detained, and the model includes court-by-year-month fixed effects and bail-judge fixed effects so that defendants arrested in an outage week are compared with defendants arrested in surrounding non-outage weeks before the same judges. The key variables are days detained (treatment), any formal employment in the year after resolution (outcome), `outage_week` (instrument, first stage of roughly 3.8 extra days), and the baseline covariates prior_arrests, charge_severity, public_defender, dv_charge, age and prior_earn, which I will use for balance tests across outage and non-outage weeks and as precision controls rather than for identification. The outage timing is mechanically unrelated to who is arrested and did not alter judge assignment, so the main identifying assumption is that a 96-hour hearing delay affects later employment only through additional detention, with standard errors clustered by arrest week, the level at which the instrument varies. I will not use `judge_leniency` even though assignment is as good as random given court-by-month fixed effects, because the caseload office uses the same leave-one-out release rate to set each judge's job-readiness program quota (one slot per 5 points) and the program enrolls defendants at random from each judge's hearings regardless of release, so lenient judges mechanically push more of their defendants into an employment program—a direct channel from the instrument to the outcome that violates the exclusion restriction. The main threat to the outage design is likewise exclusion: the delay could affect employment through disrupted case processing, plea timing, or record-keeping during outage weeks, or arrest composition could differ during outages, so I will check that `outage_week` does not predict pre-arrest earnings, charge mix, program enrollment, or disposition type, and I will show the reduced form and first stage directly. The resulting estimate is a local average treatment effect for defendants whose detention is lengthened by a few days at the bail-hearing margin, so it speaks to short additional spells rather than to the effect of months-long detention.

CANDIDATES:
judge_leniency | violated
outage_week | plausible
INSTRUMENT: outage_week

**Plan.** I will estimate the effect of years of charter enrollment on 8th-grade math scores by two-stage least squares, instrumenting years enrolled with `second_draw_offer` in the subsample of applicants who received no initial offer and were entered in the September second draw, with fixed effects for each second-draw lottery cell (school by grade by year) and `baseline_math`, `frl`, and `parent_college` as precision controls. The second draw is an independent random lottery, so within cells the offer is as good as randomly assigned and shifts enrollment by about 0.6 years, giving a usable first stage; I will verify balance of `baseline_math`, `frl`, `parent_college`, `dist_charter`, `n_ranked`, and `sibling_charter` across second-draw winners and losers. I will not use `lottery_offer` despite its randomization and stronger first stage (0.9 years), because every initial-offer holder was placed on the May confirmed placement roster whether or not they enrolled, and the roster automatically enrolls students in the district's free grades 6–8 math tutoring program, so the initial offer moves math scores through a channel other than charter attendance and violates the exclusion restriction, with no tutoring variable available to net it out. Second-draw winners are not exposed to this channel because the roster closes in May and accepts no later additions, so neither winners nor losers in the second-draw sample receive roster-based tutoring. `dist_charter`, `sibling_charter`, and `n_ranked` are rejected as instruments because they reflect residential sorting and family preferences that plausibly affect math scores directly, so they serve only as covariates and balance checks. The main threat is differential attrition: if winning a second-draw seat changes whether a student remains in the state testing system through 8th grade (e.g., losers leaving the district), the comparison is contaminated, so I will report follow-up rates by offer status and bound the effect under worst-case attrition, while acknowledging that the smaller second-draw sample and 0.6-year first stage reduce power and that the LATE applies to second-draw compliers rather than all applicants.

CANDIDATES:
lottery_offer | violated
second_draw_offer | plausible
dist_charter | doubtful
sibling_charter | doubtful
n_ranked | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: second_draw_offer

Identification: I will instrument the 2014 household broadband subscription share with crew_order, the lottery-drawn month (0-11) of fiber-crew arrival among the 104 phase-3 districts, estimating a just-identified 2SLS of the district 11th-grade score on instrumented subscription share, with robust standard errors and the baseline covariates (median_income, rural_share, per_pupil, college_share, enroll) included only for precision after checking they are balanced across crew_order. I will not use fiber_phase even though it was also randomized and has a stronger first stage (-4 pp per phase), because a district's phase also fixed the year it joined the connected-districts list and therefore how many years of school technology-fund money (classroom laptops and computer labs) it had received by 2014, a direct channel to test scores that violates the exclusion restriction. Within phase 3 every district joined the list at the same time, so crew_order shifts only when fiber was installed and should move scores only through household subscriptions. Key variables are the outcome score, the subscription-share treatment, crew_order as instrument, fiber_phase to define the phase-3 analysis sample, and the baseline covariates for balance tests; I will also report the reduced form (score on crew_order) and the first-stage F. The main threat is weak identification and low power: the first stage is only 1 pp per month in 104 districts, so I will report Anderson-Rubin confidence sets, and I will probe exclusion by checking that earlier crew arrival did not also change school-side connectivity or other district inputs. dist_datacenter is a non-random geographic variable likely correlated with rurality and income, so I rule it out as an instrument.

CANDIDATES:
fiber_phase | violated
crew_order | plausible
dist_datacenter | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: crew_order

Identification strategy: I will estimate a just-identified 2SLS (Wald) design on the subsample of families offered a voucher (voucher_lottery = 1), instrumenting years the child lived in a voucher unit before 18 with intake_team, the housing-authority software's random routing of lease-up paperwork to the fast (2-week) intake team, which raises tenure by about 2.0 years because fewer families gave up before leasing. Key variables: outcome = child earnings at age 26 from tax records; treatment = years in a voucher-subsidized unit before 18; instrument = intake_team; voucher_lottery to define the sample; and the baseline application-date covariates (hh_income97, n_children, tract_poverty, parent_employed, child_age97, public_housing) for balance tests and precision, with standard errors clustered by family since siblings share the assignment. I will not use voucher_lottery as the instrument even though it was randomly drawn and strongly shifts tenure (4.2 years), because every family on the 2003 offer roster also had a parent enrolled in the county's free two-year job-training program, so the lottery moves children's earnings through a parental-employment channel that bypasses voucher tenure and violates exclusion; restricting to offered families holds that job-training exposure constant, so the intake_team contrast is clean of it. The main threat is exclusion for intake_team: a 2-week versus 9-week processing lag may change not only whether a family leases up but also where it leases (search time, neighborhood and unit quality), so the estimate is a LATE for marginal lease-up families and would attribute any neighborhood-quality effect to tenure; I will check covariate balance across teams, confirm the instrument predicts lease-up timing but no pre-assignment characteristic, and report the reduced form alongside the IV. I will not add the follow-up, imputed, suppressed, or post-treatment codebook variables as controls, since they are measured after assignment or mechanically depend on treatment, regardless of how clean the file is.

CANDIDATES:
voucher_lottery | violated
intake_team | plausible
INSTRUMENT: intake_team

I will estimate the effect of military service on 1981 Social Security earnings by two-stage least squares, restricting the sample to draft-eligible men whose induction files were held at the regional induction station that burned in 1970 and using `station_delay` (weeks of lottery-ordered file-rebuilding delay, 0 to 25) as the instrument for the service indicator. The first stage regresses service on `station_delay` with birth-year fixed effects (each week of delay lowers service by about 1.2 percentage points, so the 25-week range shifts service rates by roughly 30 points, giving a strong first stage), and the second stage regresses 1981 earnings on predicted service with the same fixed effects, reporting the reduced form alongside the IV estimate. I will not use `low_number` as the instrument because the state civil service awarded five hiring-preference points on every public-sector application to every draft-eligible man whether or not he served, a direct channel from lottery eligibility to earnings that violates the exclusion restriction; within the burned-station subsample every man is draft-eligible, so the hiring preference is held constant and cannot contaminate the delay instrument. I will verify that the lottery-ordered delay is as good as random by testing balance of `earn_1968`, `educ_1970`, `married_1970`, `race`, `birth_state`, and `father_occ` across weeks of delay, adding them as controls only for precision. The main threat is the exclusion restriction for the delay itself: a longer wait in 1970 could have shifted the timing of schooling or civilian job entry and affected 1981 earnings through channels other than service, and because the instrument exists only for one station's draft-eligible men, the estimate is a local effect for those compliers that may be imprecise and not generalize to all draftees.

CANDIDATES:
low_number | violated
station_delay | plausible
INSTRUMENT: station_delay

I will estimate the effect of class size on class-average reading scores by instrumental variables, using split_audit (the ministry's 1991 random audit draw that forced selected schools to add one class beyond what the 40-student cap requires) as the instrument for actual class size, with grade dummies, a smooth function of enroll_grade, and baseline covariates (prior_score, pct_disadv, town_size, religious, teacher_exp) as controls, and standard errors clustered by school. Because the audit was a random draw and "changed nothing else," it is independent of potential outcomes and satisfies exclusion; its first stage (audited grades 3.1 students smaller) is sizable, and because the audit-added class is not one the cap requires, it does not trigger the remedial reading-hours grant. I reject the Maimonides-style fuzzy RD/IV on rule_size, despite its strong first stage (0.7) and unmanipulable register enrollment, because the ministry's grant gives 2 extra weekly reading hours for each class beyond the first that the cap requires, so the same discontinuities at 40, 80, and 120 that shift class size also shift reading instruction, a direct channel to the reading outcome that violates exclusion and cannot be absorbed by controls since the grant is collinear with the discontinuity. Raw enroll_grade is not a valid instrument either, since enrollment tracks school size, urbanicity, and disadvantage that affect scores directly, so it enters only as a smooth control. I will verify the randomization by testing covariate and prior_score balance across split_audit and report the first-stage F. The main threat is that a single binary instrument on a modest number of audited grades yields an imprecise estimate that is sensitive to whether the audit truly altered nothing else (e.g., heightened scrutiny changing teaching or reporting), so I will report Anderson-Rubin confidence intervals and check that audited and non-audited grades do not differ on other class-level variables.

CANDIDATES:
rule_size | violated
split_audit | plausible
enroll_grade | violated
INSTRUMENT: split_audit

I will estimate the effect of class size on class-average reading scores by two-stage least squares, instrumenting actual class size with split_audit, the indicator for grades in schools that the ministry's 1991 random audit draw required to add one class beyond what the 40-student cap requires; because the draw was random it is independent of school and class characteristics, and it moves class size by about 3.1 students, so the first stage is strong. Key variables are actual class size (treatment), class average reading score (outcome), and split_audit (instrument), with enroll_grade (as a smooth function), grade, pct_disadv, prior_score, town_size, religious, and teacher_exp used only as precision controls and balance checks, and standard errors clustered by school since the audit was assigned at the school level. I will not use rule_size (Maimonides'-rule predicted size) as the instrument: the supplementary remedial reading-hours grant gives every class 2 extra weekly reading hours for each class beyond the first recorded in the ministry's staffing file, and that file records exactly the cap-required class count that generates rule_size, so the predicted-size drops at enrollment 40, 80, and 120 coincide with jumps in reading instruction that raise reading scores directly, violating the exclusion restriction for this outcome regardless of how flexibly enrollment is controlled. The audit-added class lies beyond the cap-required count recorded in the staffing file, so it does not trigger the grant, and the documentation states the audit changed nothing else at those schools. The main threat is exclusion or independence failing for split_audit if the extra audit class were in fact recorded in the staffing file (and so pulled in grant hours) or if 1991 audited schools differ in survival into the analysis sample, so I will test covariate and prior_score balance across split_audit, check that cap-required class counts (and any grant receipt) are unchanged by audit status, and report the rule_size estimate only as a sensitivity bound flagged as biased toward finding benefits of smaller classes.

CANDIDATES:
rule_size | violated
split_audit | plausible
INSTRUMENT: split_audit

I will estimate the effect of military service on 1981 Social Security earnings by two-stage least squares, instrumenting "served" with `station_delay` — the lottery-drawn number of weeks (0–25) by which a man's induction was postponed while clerks rebuilt the files destroyed in the 1970 induction-station fire — on the subsample of draft-eligible men whose files were held at that station, the only men for whom the variable is defined. Because the order of file reconstruction was drawn by lottery, the delay is independent of potential earnings, and it has a usable first stage (each week lowers the probability of service by about 1.2 points, so the full range shifts service by up to roughly 30 points); I will report the first stage, the reduced form, and the IV estimate, with birth-year fixed effects and pre-treatment covariates (educ_1970, race, birth_state, father_occ, earn_1968, married_1970) included for precision and used to check covariate balance across delay lengths. I will not use `low_number` as an instrument despite its random assignment and 15-point first stage, because the documentation shows it violates exclusion: every man with a number at or below the ceiling was entered on the Selective Service class 1-A register, and the state civil service awards five hiring-preference points on every public-sector application to every man on that register whether or not he served, so draft eligibility affects earnings directly; within the station-delay subsample all men are draft-eligible, so this channel is held constant rather than confounding the estimate. The key variables are therefore served (treatment), 1981 earnings (outcome), station_delay (instrument), low_number (sample-definition variable and rejected instrument), birth-year indicators, and the pre-1970 covariates; the several hundred auto-generated "items" variables describe post-2013 administrative records and are irrelevant to a 1981 outcome, so I will not use them. The main threat is that the estimate is a local average treatment effect for a small, single-station group of men whose service hinged on a few months' delay, so power will be limited and generalizability narrow; a secondary threat is a direct effect of the delay itself (e.g., through the timing of service or of civilian labor-market entry) that would violate exclusion, which I will probe by testing whether delay predicts pre-treatment covariates and whether the reduced form is approximately monotone in weeks of delay.

CANDIDATES:
low_number | violated
station_delay | plausible
INSTRUMENT: station_delay

I will estimate the effect of Medicaid enrollment on 18-month emergency department visits with two-stage least squares, instrumenting months enrolled with `slow_team`, the random routing of returned applications to the caseworker team that was six weeks slower during the 2008 staffing transition, estimated on the subsample of lottery-selected applicants for whom `slow_team` is non-missing. The first stage regresses months enrolled on `slow_team` (expected roughly -2.0 months), the second stage relates the ED visit count to instrumented enrollment, and I will include `age08`, `hh_size`, `prior_ed`, `chronic`, `urban`, and `english` as precision controls after first confirming they are balanced across the two teams, which is the direct test that routing was in fact random. I will not use `lottery_selected` as the instrument even though selection was random (within household-size strata) and the first stage is strong (3.4 months), because the state mailed every selected person a voucher for free community primary-care visits whether or not they enrolled, so selection shifts ED use through a non-Medicaid channel and the exclusion restriction fails; I will report the lottery reduced form only as the effect of the combined "Medicaid chance plus clinic voucher" package, and the fact that all applicants in the `slow_team` sample received the voucher means it does not contaminate the within-applicant comparison. The main threat is that the slow team may have differed in more than processing speed, for example in denial rates, eligibility lapses, or communication with applicants that independently changed care-seeking, which would violate exclusion, so I will check that the two teams applied identical approval rules and had identical approval rates, and that the 18-month outcome window is anchored to the lottery or application date rather than the approval date so the delay does not mechanically shift the observation period. Because the estimate is a LATE for applicants whose enrollment duration was moved by processing delay, I will state clearly that it does not generalize to the non-applicant margin and will report the complier share and a Poisson-IV robustness check for the count outcome.

CANDIDATES:
lottery_selected | violated
slow_team | plausible
INSTRUMENT: slow_team

I will estimate the causal effect of holding a microloan on monthly business profits (three years post-branch) by two-stage least squares, using `officer_slots` — the lender's 2007 randomized assignment of an extra loan officer to a branch — as the instrument, restricting the sample to the roughly 10,000 households in the 52 branch neighborhoods where it is defined. The first stage regresses the microloan indicator on `officer_slots` (a 12-percentage-point uptake shift), the second stage regresses profits on predicted loan-holding, with baseline covariates (`biz_2005`, `head_educ`, `hh_size`, `assets`, `slum`, `dist_market`) for precision and balance checks, and standard errors clustered by neighborhood because assignment was at the branch level. The instrument is credible because it was randomized (independence), loan officers only process loan applications so the extra officer can move profits only by changing who gets a loan (exclusion), and the city's free business-skills course was open to every resident of all 52 branch neighborhoods, so it is held constant within this estimation sample rather than correlated with the instrument. I reject `branch_area` despite its randomization and stronger 20-point first stage: the business-skills course was rolled out only in branch neighborhoods the month each branch opened, giving branch assignment a direct path to business profits that bypasses the loan, so its exclusion restriction fails and a `branch_area` IV would bundle loan effects with training effects (I will report the `branch_area` reduced form only as the ITT of the branch-plus-course package). The main threat is a weak, coarsely clustered first stage — a 12-point uptake shift randomized across only 52 branches gives limited power and weak-instrument risk — so I will report the first-stage F, use Anderson–Rubin weak-IV-robust confidence intervals with a wild cluster bootstrap, and test baseline balance across `officer_slots`. A secondary caveat is that the estimate is a LATE for households induced to borrow by faster loan processing, and I will verify from the lender's records that the pilot did not alter other branch practices such as loan sizes; the numbered administrative variables are not used because their documentation (2013 migration, 2014 definition changes, nominal dollars) is inconsistent with a 2006–2009 rupee-denominated study.

CANDIDATES:
branch_area | violated
officer_slots | plausible
INSTRUMENT: officer_slots

I will estimate the effect of months enrolled in Medicaid on ED visits in the following 18 months with a two-stage least squares design that uses `slow_team` as the instrument: among lottery-selected people who returned an application, routing to the slow caseworker team was random during the 2008 staffing transition and lowers enrollment by 2.0 months, so the reduced-form difference in ED visits between slow-team and fast-team applicants, scaled by that first stage, identifies a LATE for applicants whose coverage duration was shifted by the delay. Months enrolled is the endogenous treatment, ED visits in the 18 months after is the outcome, and I will include `hh_size` fixed effects and baseline controls (`age08`, `prior_ed`, `chronic`, `urban`, `english`) only for precision, after verifying that these covariates are balanced across teams and that the first-stage F-statistic is strong. I will not use `lottery_selected` as the instrument even though it was randomized and has a larger first stage (3.4 months), because everyone selected, and no one else, was placed on the 2008 outreach mailing list and mailed a voucher for free community primary-care visits, which can reduce ED use directly and therefore violates the exclusion restriction for Medicaid enrollment; I will report the lottery reduced form (with household-size fixed effects) only as the intention-to-treat effect of the bundled selection-plus-voucher package. Because every person in the `slow_team` analysis sample was lottery-selected, the voucher channel is held constant within the IV sample rather than confounding it. The main threat is the exclusion restriction for `slow_team` itself: a six-week approval delay could change ED visits through channels other than total months enrolled, such as shifting when coverage begins within the 18-month window, differential denial rates or communication by the slow team, or uninsured ED use during the wait, so I will test whether the two teams differ on approval rates and baseline characteristics and interpret the estimate as the effect of enrollment duration among applicants, not the full lottery population.

CANDIDATES:
